title: Collaudemus Magdalenae

content:
Full of grace are thy lips.
Because God hath blessed thee forever.

Mary, weep not, weep no longer,
Now thy heart hath gained its goal;
Here, in truth, the Gardener standeth,
But the Gardener of thy soul,
Who within thy spirit's garden
By his love hath made thee whole.

Now from grief and lamentation
Lift thy drooping heart with cheer;
While for love of him thou mournest,
Lo, thy Lord regained is here!
Fainting for him, thou hast found him;
All unknown, behold him near!

Whence thy sorrow, whence thy weeping,
Since with thee true bliss abides?
In thy heart, though undiscovered,
Balm of consolation hides:
Holding all, thou canst no longer
Lack the cure that Health provides.

Nay, no wonder if she knows not
Till the Sower's seed be sown,
Till from him, the word eternal,
Light within her heart is thrown.
Now he calls her, and 'Rabboni,'
She in turn her Lord doth own.

Faith that washed the feet of Jesus,
Fed with dew the Fount of Grace
Win for us a like compassion,
That, with all the ransomed race,
At the glory of his rising
We may see him face to face!

Glory be to God and honour,
Who, preferring sacrifice,
Far above the rich man's bounty,
Sweetness found in Mary's sighs,
Who for all, his love foretasting,
Spreads the banquet of the skies.
Amen.
title: O Maria, noli flere

content:
God hath chosen and forechosen her.
He hath made her to dwell in his tabernacle.

Lord of Creation, bow thine ear, O Christ, to hear
        The intercession of thy servant true and dear,
        That we unworthy, who have trespassed in thy sight,
        May live before thee where he dwells in glorious light.

        Twin lamps, adorning heaven's eternal palaces!
        James, with thy brother John, divine evangelist!
        Entreat that pardon for his lowly suppliants,
        Which Christ hath freely promised to the penitent.

        O God our Saviour, look on thine inheritance,
        Sealed by the favour shining from thy countenance;
        That no false spirit bring to nought the souls of price
        Bought by the merit of thy perfect Sacrifice.

        We bear the burden of our guilt and enmity,
        Until thy pardon lift the heart from slavery;
        Then through the spending of thy life-blood, King of grace,
        Grant us unending triumph in thy holy place.

        To thee the glorious Christ, our Saviour manifest,
        All wreaths victorious, praise and worship be addrest,
        Whom with the living Father humbly we adore,
        And the life-giving Spirit, God for evermore. Amen.
title: Annue Christe saeculorum Domine

content:
The morning star succeeds to night,
The dawn soon follows, growing white,
The herald in the sunrise bright
The floods the waking world with light.

Christ is the sun of righteousness,
The dawn, the Mother full of grace;
Bright Anne precedes her like the star,
To drive the shades of law afar.

Lo, Anne; the very fruitful root,
The tree of healing, when a shoot
To richest blossoming did spring,
And brought us Christ, to whom we sing:

All honour, praise, and glory be,
O Jesus, Virgin-born, to thee;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father, and to Paraclete. Amen.
title: Succedit nocti lucifer

content:
The just exult in their glory.
They shout for joy on their beds.

        The intercession of thy servant true and dear,

content:
Let all the Saints in concert sing,
The mother of that Maid to laud
By whose unistained childbearing
Salvation came to men from God.

She sought her faithful progeny
From God the Father, Lord of light;
And merited most worthily
The pride of Virgins, Mary bright.

To Joachim, esteemed the peer
Of any in his goodliness,
Anne brought forth Mary, Mother dear
Of Jesus, King of righteousness.

Let Jesse's noble stock efface
From Mother Eve her olden taints:
Anne bears her child, the child of grace,
The fairest blossom of the Saints!

All honour, praise, and glory be,
O Jesus, Virgin-born, to thee;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father, and to Paraclete. Amen.
title: Omnis sanctorum

content:
The just exult in their glory.
They shout for joy on their beds.

Christ's noble servants, we would sing your greatness!
How ye wrought wonders in your faith so steadfast!
Earth in your honour now doth join in heaven's
Endless rejoicings.

Ye too were mortal, like to us your brethren,
Yet did ye serve God with such humble valour
That now, immortal, ye on high in glory
With Christ are reigning.

From your high places look on earth's great sorrows;
Pray for the mourners, for the sick and ailing;
Help the sin-stricken; bring to pain-racked bodies
Comfort and healing.

Thus will our hymns, your charity declaring,
Praise God's own goodness for your prayerful succour,
Whilst still ye stretch forth loving hands to aid us
In our aspiring.

Glory and virtue, honour and salvation,
Be unto him that, sitting in the highest,
Governeth all things, Lord and God Almighty,
Trinity blessed. Amen.
title: Inclitos Christi

content:
The secret of the Lord is among them that fear him, and he will show them his covenant.
Yea, gracious and righteous is the Lord.

Author of all things, Christ, the world's Redeemer,
Monarch of Monarchs, judgement's dream awarder,
Now to our praises, as to our petitions,
Graciously hearken.

While the night fleeteth, we our votive anthems
Frame to thine honour; grant that they may please thee;
And as we hymn thee, source of Light eternal,
Ever refresh us.

Sunlike thy visage shone with rays of splendour,
Brightly thy raiment gleamed with snowy whiteness,
When mid the Prophets, Moses and Elias,
Thou wast transfigured.

Then did the Father own thee Sole-begotten;
Thou art the glory of the holy Angels;
Thee, the way, virtue, life, the world's Salvation,
Ever confess we.

Glory and power be to thee, Creator,
Who alone all things rulest and controllest,
Throned in thy kingdom, Monarch everlasting,
Trinal and Onely. Amen.
reference: The Dedication of the Basilica of Saint Mary Major
title: O sator rerum

content:
A crown of gold is set upon his head.
Wherein is engraved holiness, glory, and honour.
reference: The Dedication of the Basilica of Saint Mary Major

content:
An image of that heavenly light,
The goal the Church keeps ay in sight,
Christ on the holy mount displays
Where he outshines the sun's bright rays.

Let every age proclaimer be
How, on this day, the chosen three
With Moses and Elias heard
The Lord speak many a gracious word.

As witnesses to grace are nigh
Those twain, the Law and Prophecy;
And to the Son, from out the cloud,
The Father's record thunders loud.

With garments whiter than the snows,
And shining face, Lord Jesus shows
What glory for those Saints shall be
Who joy in God with piety.

The vision and the mystery
Make faithful hearts beat quick and high,
So on this solemn day of days
The cry goes up of prayer and praise.

O God the Father, God the Son,
And Holy Spirit, Three in One,
Vouchsafe to bring us, by thy grace,
To see thy glory face to face. Amen.
reference: The Dedication of the Basilica of Saint Mary Major
title: Caelestis formarm gloriae

content:
Glorious didst thou appear in the sight of the Lord.
Because the Lord hath clothed thee with majesty.
reference: The Dedication of the Basilica of Saint Mary Major

content:
O Light of light, by love inclined,
Jesu, Redeemer of mankind,
With loving-kindness deign to hear
From suppliant voices praise and prayer.

Thou who to raise our souls from hell
Didst deign in fleshly form to dwell,
Vouchsafe us, when our race is run,
In thy fair Body to be one.

More bright than day thy face did show,
Thy raiment whiter than the snow,
When on the mount to mortals blest
Man's Maker thou was manifest.

Two prophets, that had faith to see,
With thine elect found company,
Where unto each, divinely shown,
The Godhead veiled in form was known.

The heavens above his glory named,
The Father's voice the Son proclaimed;
To whom, the King of glory now,
All faithful hearts adoring bow.

May all who seek thy praise aright
Through purer lives show forth thy light;
So to the brightness of the skies
By holy deeds our hearts shall rise.

Eternal God, to thee we raise,
The King of kings, our hymn of praise,
Who Three in One and One in Three
Doth live and reign eternally. Amen.

content:
Glorious didst thou appear in the sight of the Lord.
Because the Lord hath clothed thee with majesty.

Virgin most holy, robed in golden sunlight,
Queen for whose crowning twelve bright stars were garnered,
Lady, enthroned, with the moon thy footstool,
Great is thy glory.

There in the presence of thy Son and Saviour,
Where death is vanquished, hell hath no dominion,
Looking upon us, Queen of earth and heaven,
For us thou prayest.

We are thy children, to thy care entrusted:
Still are we threatened by the ancient serpent,
Still then, O Mother, may thy intercession
Aid and defend us.

Pray that the faithful find divine protection,
Pray that the erring to the fold be gathered,
Pray that the heathen, freed from death's dark shadow,
Come to salvation.

May thy entreaty win for sinners pardon,
Comfort for mourners, strength for all the needy;
Lighten our pathway, star of hope above us,
Still as we struggle.

God who hath crowned thee with a crown of glory,
One in Three Persons, him we praise for ever,
Who in his mercy chose thee for our Mother,
Virgin most blessed. Amen.
reference: The Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary
title: Solis, o Virgo

content:
Thou art exalted, O holy Mother of God.
Above the choir of Angels, unto the heavenly kingdom.
reference: The Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary

content:
Blest Maid, to highest dignity
Ordained by God eternally,
Forechosen by decree divine
To bear his Son, to call him thine.

The devil's ancient enmity
Won no dominion over thee:
With sin thy soul was never stained,
God's grave alone therein has reigned.

That Adam's loss he might retrieve
Thou didst our very life conceive:
Flesh of thy flesh, he came to give
Himself that we through him might live.

Now death, our sinful race's dower,
No more can hold thee in its power;
Thou to the heavenly courts dost fly
To join thy gracious Son on high.

Such wondrous glories on thee rest,
Nature itself with thee is blest;
Thy holy calling was its own,
It share with thee thine honoured throne.

Then to us exiles turn thine eyes,
Fair Queen, triumphant in the skies;
Till, aided by thy prayer, we see.
Our blessed fatherland with thee.

All honour, laud, and glory be,
O Jesu, Virgin-born, to thee,
Whom with the Father we adore,
And Holy Ghost, for evermore. Amen.
reference: The Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary
title: O prima, Virgo

content:
Thou art exalted, O holy Mother of God.
Above the choir of Angels, unto the heavenly kingdom.
reference: The Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary

content:
Come rejoicing,
Faithful men, with rapture singing
Alleluia!

Monarch's Monarch,
From a holy maiden springing,
Mighty wonder!

Angel of the Counsel here,
Sun from star, he doth appear,
Born of maiden:

He a sun who knows no night,
She a star whose paler light
Fadeth never.

As a star its kindred ray,
Mary doth her Child display,
Like in nature;

Still undimmed the star shines on,
And the maiden bears a Son,
Pure as ever.

Lebanon his cedar tall
To the hyssop on the wall
Lowly bendeth;

From the highest, him we name
Word of God, to human frame
Now descendeth.

Yet the synagogue denied
What Esaias had descried:
Blindness fell upon the guide,
Proud unheeding.

If her Prophets speak in vain,
Let her heed a Gentile strain,
And, from mystic Sibyl, gain
Light and leading.

No longer then delay,
Hear what the Scriptures say,
Why be cast away
A race forlorn?

Turn and this Child behold,
That very Son, of old
In God's writ foretold,
A Maid hath borne. Amen.
reference: The Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary
title: Laetabundus

content:
Thou art exalted, O holy Mother of God.
Above the choir of Angels, unto the heavenly kingdom.
reference: The Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary

content:
Lord of Creation, bow thine ear, O Christ, to hear
        The intercession of thy servant true and dear,
        That we unworthy, who have trespassed in thy sight,
        May live before thee where he dwells in glorious light.

        May thy petitions, golden star, Bartholomew,
        Whose light the sunbeams far exceeds in brilliancy,
        Raise souls beclouded to celestial purity,
        And heal the sickness of our guilty consciences.

        O God our Saviour, look on thine inheritance,
        Sealed by the favour shining from thy countenance;

title: Annue Christe saeculorum Domine

content:
Of Angles once Apostle thou,
Companion of the Angels now,
O Gregory, protect our race
By faith in Christ restored to grace.

Earth's wealth and riches thou didst spurn,
And from its dazzling glory turn,
1o follow, needy, Christ the King,
Like him, too, lacking everything.

On outstretched hand thou dost bestow
Two coins, -a silver dish, -when lo!
'Neath shipwrecked, sorry garb concealed,
A noble Angel stands revealed.

Thenceforth Christ sets thee o'er his fold
His Church to rule, his place to hold;
To Peter's honours thou art led,
For in his steps thou firm didst tread.

Thy words as honey sweet impart
A strength that conquers every heart;
Than fragrant perfume stronger still,
The wisdom that thy lips distil.

With wondrous skill thou dost unfold
Of holy writ the depths untold:
The mysteries of divinity
The truth himself did teach to thee.

O thou, who Peter's charge didst share,
The Apostles' crown alike dost wear,
Now set us free from bonds of sin
That throne in heaven we too may win.

O pontiff, high above all praise,
The Church's light in thousand ways,
O leave us not in dangers sore,
Once taught and guided by thy lore.

All praise to God the Father be,
All praise, eternal Son, to thee,
All equal glory, as is meet,
To God the Holy Paraclete. Amen.

content:
The God whom earth, and sea, and sky,
        Adore, and laud, and magnify,
        Who o’er their threefold fabric reigns,
        The Virgin’s spotless womb contains.

        The God whose will by moon and sun
        And all things in due course is done,
        Is borne upon a Maiden’s breast,
        By fullest heavenly grace possest.

        How blest the Mother, in whose shrine
        The great Artificer Divine,
        Whose hand contains the earth and sky,
        Vouchsafed, as in his ark, to lie!

        Blest, in the message Gabriel brough;
        Blest, by the work the Spirit wrought:
        From whom the Great Desire of earth
        Took human flesh and human birth.

        All honour, laud, and glory be,
        O Jesu, Virgin-born, to thee!
        All glory, as is ever meet,
        To Father and to Paraclete. Amen.
title: Quem terra, pontus, aethera

content:
Today is the Nativity of the holy Virgin Mary.
Whose glorious life illumineth all the churches.

Hail, O Star that pointest
        Towards the port of heaven;
        Thou to whom as Maiden
        God for Son was given.

        When the salutation
        Gabriel had spoken.
        Peace was shed upon us,
        Eva's bonds were broken.

        Bound by Satan's fetters,
        Health and vision needing,
        God will aid and light us
        At thy gentle pleading.

        Jesu's tender Mother,
        Make thy supplication
        Unto him who chose thee
        At his Incarnation;

        That, O matchless Maiden,
        Passing meek and lowly,
        Thy dear Son may make us
        Blameless, chaste and holy.

        So, as now we journey,
        Aid our weak endeavour,
        Till we gaze on Jesus,
        And rejoice for ever.

        Father, Son, and Spirit,
        Three in One confessing,
        Give we equal glory,
        Equal praise and blessing.
        Amen.
title: Ave, maris stella

content:
Sing, my tongue, the glorious battle,
Sing the ending of the fray;
Now above the Cross, the trophy,
Sound the loud triumphant lay;
Tell how Christ, the world's Redeemer,
As a Victim won the day.

God in pity saw man fallen,
Shamed and sunk in misery,
When he fell of death by tasting
Fruit of the forbidden tree;
Then another Tree was chosen,
Which the world from sin should free.

Thus the scheme of our salvation
Was of old in order laid,
That the manifold deceiver's
Art by art might be outweighed.
And the lure the foe put forward
Into means of healing made.

Therefore when the appointed fulness
Of the holy time was come,
He was sent who maketh all things
Forth from God's eternal home;
Thus he came to earth, incarnate,
Offspring of a maiden's womb.

To the Trinity be glory
Everlasting, as is meet;
Equal to the Father, equal
To the Son and Paraclete:
Trinal Unity, whose praises
All created things repeat. Amen.
title: Pange lingua gloriosi proelium certaminis

content:
We adore thee, O Christ, and we bless thee.
Because by thy Cross thou hast redeemed the world.

Fulfilled is all that David told.
In true prophetic song of old;
Amidst the nations, God, saith he,
Hath reigned and triumphed from the Tree.

O Tree of beauty, Tree of Light!
O Tree with royal purple dight,
Elect on whose triumphal breast
Those holy limbs should find their rest:

On whose dear arms, so widely flung,
The weight of this world's ransom hung:
The price of humankind to pay,
And spoil the spoiler of his prey.

Kneel for this verse:
O Cross, our one reliance, hail!
So may thy power with us avail
To give new virtue to the saint,
And pardon to the penitent,

To thee, eternal Three in One,
Let homage meet by all be done:
Whom by the Cross thou dost restore,
Preserve and govern evermore. Amen.

        The intercession of thy servant true and dear,

        May live before thee where he dwells in glorious light.

        May saintly Matthew, high in twofold dignity
        To thee, O Jesu, plead with prayer importunate:
        So' mid life's tempests may thy guidance succour us;
        Lest death hereafter whelm us everlasting.

        O God our Saviour, look on thine inheritance,
        Sealed by the favour shining from thy countenance;

        Bought by the merit of thy perfect Sacrifice.

        Then through the spending of thy life-blood, King of grace,
        Grant us unending triumph in thy holy place.

        Whom with the living Father humbly we adore,
        And the life-giving Spirit, God for evermore. Amen.

Eternal ruler of the sky,
All things thou hast created lie
Within thy hand, nor pass they thence,
God of eternal providence.

So, sinful though thy people be,
Be with them, as they pray to thee,
And as the shade of night depart,
Shed thy new Light in every heart.

Thy holy Angel still be near,
Chosen for our protection here;
And may his ever-watchful care
Preserve us from each sinful snare.

May he our guardian ever be
Against the devil's trickery,
Lest we should, with unheeding mind
Be in those crafty toils entwined.

He from our fatherland drive far
The fear of foes, the dread of war;
May he preserve our civic peace,
And cause all pestilence to cease.

To God the Father praise be done;
He, who redeemed us by his Son
And poured on us the Holy Ghost,
Preserve us with his Angel host. Amen.

Even before the Angels will I sing praise unto thee, O my God.
I will worship toward thy holy temple, and praise thy Name.

Angelic guardians blest,
In your high praise we' sing,
And hymn the mighty aid
Ye from our Father bring,
To help our nature frail,
Lest we in danger's hour
Fall by our foes' deceiving power.

For as through woeful sin
The angel traitor fell,
To lose the bliss of heaven
In endless night of hell,
With burning envy still
He seeks to draw astray
The souls God calls to endless day.

Then with thy sleepless watch,
O guardian true, be near,
To whom the Lord entrusts
His land for ever dear,
Keep from our souls all ills,
Make thou all harm to cease,
Preserve our people still in peace.

All honour be to God,
One holy Trinity,
The threefold world is ruled
By his divinity,
Who throned in glory reigns,
And shall throughout all days:
To him be everlasting praise.
Amen.

O Christ, bestow; thy servants spare;

Regard the blessed Virgin's prayer.

Bright Angels, happy evermore,
Who in your circles nine ascend,
As ye have guarded us before,
So may ye still our steps defend.

While Prophets and Apostles high
Forgiveness for our sins entreat.
Lord, hear thy servants as they cry,
And spare us at thy judgement seat.

In purple clad, the Martyr band,
Confessors too, a shining train,
All call us to our native land,
From this our exile, back again.

Ye choirs of Virgins, wise and chaste
O may we share your seats on high,
With hermits, who from deserts waste
Were called to mansions in the sky.

So may the realms of faith be blest,
So unbelief be chased away,
Till all within one fold find rest,
Secure beneath one shepherd's sway.

To God the Father glory be,
And to his sole-begotten Son,
And glory, Holy Ghost, to thee,
While everlasting ages run. Amen.

Saint of God, elect and precious,
Protomartyr Stephen, bright
With thy love of amplest measure,
Shining round thee like a light;
Who to God commendest, dying,
Them that did thee all despite:

Glitters now the crown above thee,
Figured in thy sacred name:
O that we, who truly love thee,
May have portion in the same;
In the dreadful day of judgement
Fearing neither sin nor shame.

Laud to God, and might, and honour,
Who with flowers of rosy dye
Crowned thy forehead, and hath placed thee
In the starry throne on high:
He direct us, he protect us,
From death's sting eternally. Amen.

content:
Under the throne of God all the Saints cry out.
Avenge our blood, O Lord our God.

Creator of the earth and sky,
Ruling the firmament on high,
Clothing the day with robes of light,
Blessing with gracious sleep the night,

That rest may comfort weary men,
And brace to useful toil again,
And soothe awhile the harassed mind,
And sorrow’s heavy load unbind:

Day sinks; we thank thee for the gift;
Night comes; and once again we lift
Our prayer and vows and hymns that we
Against all ills may shielded be.

Thee let the secret heart acclaim,
Thee let our tuneful voices name,
Round thee our chaste affections cling,
Thee sober reason own as King.

That when black darkness closes day,
And shadows thicken round our way,
Faith may no darkness know, and night
From faith’s clear beam may borrow light.

Rest now, my heaven-born mind and will;
Rest, all ye thoughts and deeds of ill;
May faith its watch unwearied keep,
And cool the dreaming warmth of sleep.

From cheats of sense, Lord, keep me free,
And let my heart’s depth dream of thee;
Let not my envious foe draw near,
To break my rest with any fear.

Pray we the Father and the Son,
And Holy Ghost: O Three in One,
Blest Trinity, whom all obey,
Guard thou thy sheep by night and day. Amen.

content: Andrew first findeth his own brother Simon, and saith unto him: we have found the Messiah: * and he brought him to Jesus.
The Holy Spirit shall come upon thee, Mary: * fear thou not to have in thy womb the Son of God, alleluia.
The voice of one crying in the wilderness: * Prepare ye the way of the Lord; make ye straight a highway for our God.
Now when John had heard in the prison the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples, and asked him, saying: * Art thou he which is to come, or look we for another?
Behold, a Virgin shall conceive, and bear a Son: * and his Name shall be called Emmanuel.

O Virgin of Virgins, * how shall this be? for neither before thee was any seen like thee, nor shall there be after.  Daughters of Jerusalem, why marvel ye at me?  The thing which ye behold is a divine mystery.
Glory * to God in the highest, and on earth peace to men of good will, alleluia, alleluia.
The ungodly ran upon him with one accord and stoned him, to give him over unto death: * but he right gladly endured the stones, that he might merit to obtain a diadem of glory, alleluia.
This is the same John, which leant upon Jesus' bosom at supper: * the blessed Apostle, unto whom were revealed the secrets of heaven.
From two years old and under, * did Herod slay all the male children, for the sake of the Lord.
Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? * Behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing. How is it that ye sought me? Wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?

A wondrous mystery is made known today; nature herself is changed:  God is made man; that which he was he remaineth, and that which he was not he becometh, suffering neither confusion nor division.  Alleluia.
And we beheld his glory, * the glory as of the Only Begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth.

Today * the Church is joined to her heavenly Bridegroom; because in Jordan Christ hath washed away her offenses: the wise men with their offerings hasten to the royal marriage, and the guests are regaled with water made wine, alleluia.

John the Forerunner rejoiceth with the river Jordan; * when the Lord was baptized, joy and gladness were come to the whole world: through the hallowing of water there came to us remission of sins; let us all beseech him, Have mercy upon us.

Andrew first findeth his own brother Simon, And Jesus, walking by the Sea of Galilee, saw Peter, and Andrew his brother, and saith unto them: * Come ye after me, and I will make you fishers of men, and straightway they forsook their nets, and likewise the ship, and followed him. * and saith unto him, We have found the Messiah: and he brought him to Jesus.

And Jesus, walking by the Sea of Galilee, saw Peter, and Andrew his brother, and saith unto them: * Come ye after me, and I will make you fishers of men, and straightway they forsook their nets, and likewise the ship, and followed him.
And they were astonished at his doctrine: * for he taught them as one that had authority, and not as the scribes.
In the morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out and departed into a solitary place: * and there prayed.

There came a leper to him, beseeching him, and kneeling down to him, and saying unto him, If thou wilt, thou canst make me clean. * And Jesus moved with compassion, put forth his hand, and touched him, and saith unto him, I will; be thou clean.
Today * the blessed Virgin Mary presented the Child Jesus in the temple; and Simeon, filled with the Holy Spirit, received him into his arms, and blessed God for ever.
The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man that is an householder: * which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard, saith the Lord.
Know ye not that they which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the prize? * So run, that ye may obtain.
Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, * and all things shall be accomplished which were written by the prophets concerning the Son of Man.
When ye fast, * be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance.
Then Joseph, * being raised from sleep, did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife.
The Angel Gabriel was sent to Mary: * a virgin espoused to Joseph.
Jesus was led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil: * and when he had fasted by the space of forty days and forty nights, he was afterward hungered.
There came a voice from heaven, and the Father's voice was heard: * This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hearken unto him.
Destroy this temple, spake the Lord, and in three days I will raise it up: * but this he said of the temple of his body.
I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, * Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee, and am no more worthy to be called thy son.
Except a grain of wheat fall into the ground and die, it abideth alone: * but if it die, it bringeth forth much fruit.
The multitudes * which came together for the feast day cried unto the Lord: Blessed is he that cometh in the Name of the Lord. Hosanna In the highest.
Now he that betrayed him * gave them a sign, saying: Whomsoever I shall kiss, that same is he; hold him fast.
They set up over his head this accusation written: * Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews.
The women, sitting over against the sepulchre, * made lamentation, weeping for the Lord.
And very early in the morning * the first day of the week, they came unto the sepulcher at the rising of the sun, alleluia.
Go quickly, * and tell his disciples that the Lord is risen from the dead, alleluia.
reference: MONDAY IN THE OCTAVE OF EASTER

content: Mary stood at the sepulchre weeping: * and seeth two Angels in white sitting, and the napkin that was about the head of Jesus, alleluia.
reference: TUESDAY IN THE OCTAVE OF EASTER

content: The Lord is risen indeed, * and hath appeared to Simon, alleluia.
reference: WEDNESDAY IN THE OCTAVE OF EASTER

content: Jesus stood in the midst of his disciples, * and said unto them: Peace be unto you, alleluia.
reference: THURSDAY IN THE OCTAVE OF EASTER

content: Cast the net * on the right side of the ship: and ye shall find, alleluia.
reference: FRIDAY IN THE OCTAVE OF EASTER

content: When Jesus was risen * early the first day of the week: he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, out of whom he had cast seven devils, alleluia.
reference: SATURDAY IN THE OCTAVE OF EASTER

content: Because thou hast seen me, Thomas, * thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed, alleluia.
Thus it is written, * and thus it behoved Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day, alleluia.
I am the Shepherd of the sheep; * I am the Way and the Truth: I am the Good Shepherd, and I know my sheep, and am known of mine, alleluia.
I am the Vine, * ye are the branches: he that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit; for without me ye can do nothing, alleluia.
Greater love hath no man than this, * that a man lay down his life for his friends, alleluia.
I ascend * unto my Father, and to your Father: and to my God, and your God, alleluia.
When the Comforter is come, * whom I will send unto you, even the Spirit of Truth, which proceedeth from the Father: he shall testify of me, alleluia.
Receive ye * the Holy Ghost: whosesoever sins ye remit, they are remitted unto them, alleluia.
The Spirit of the Lord: * hath filled all the world, alleluia.
Suddenly there came a sound from heaven * as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting, alleluia.
They were all filled with the Holy Ghost, * and began to speak, alleluia.
The Apostles did speak with other tongues: * the wonderful works of God, alleluia.
They were all filled with the Holy Ghost, * and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.
And the twelve Apostles  departed, * and went through the villages: preaching the Gospel, and healing everywhere, alleluia, alleluia.
Blessed be * the holy Creator and Governor of all things, the holy and undivided Trinity, both now and ever, and to endless ages of ages.
I am * the living bread, which came down from heaven: if any man eat of this bread, he shall live forever, alleluia.
Beloved, let us love one another: * for love is of God, and everyone that loveth is born of God and knoweth God.
Through his tender mercies * God hath visited us and redeemed his people.  Alleluia.
We know the love of God, * because he laid down his life for us: and we ought to lay down our lives for the brethren.
All of you be subject one to another, * and be clothed with humility: for God resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble.
The sufferings of this present time: * are not worthy to be compared with the glory that shall be revealed unto us.
Be ye all of one mind, * having compassion one of another: love as brethren; be pitiful, be courteous.
Now if we died with Christ: * we believe that we shall also live with him.
The wages of sin is death: * but the free gift of God is eternal life, through Jesus Christ our Lord.
As many as are led * by the Spirit of God: they are the sons of God.
There hath no temptation taken you: * but such as is common to man.
No man can say * that Jesus is Lord: but by the Holy Ghost.
Brethren, * I declare unto you the Gospel which I preached unto you: and wherein ye stand.
Such trust have we * through Christ to Godward: not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think anything of ourselves, but our sufficiency is from God.
Walk in the Spirit: * and ye shall not fulfil the desire of the flesh.
If we live in the Spirit: * let us also walk in the Spirit.
God forbid that I should glory, * save in the Cross of our Lord Jesus Christ: by whom the world is crucified unto me, and I unto the world.
That you may be able to know * the love of Christ which passeth knowledge: and be filled with all the fullness of God.
Walk worthy of the vocation * wherewith ye are called: with lowliness and meekness, forbearing one another in love.
I thank my God * always on your behalf: for the grace of God which is given you by Jesus Christ.
Be ye kind one to another, * forgiving one another: even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you.
Walk circumspectly, * not as fools but as wise: redeeming the time, because the days are evil.
Be ye strong in the Lord: * and in the power of his might.
May ye be filled with the fruits of righteousness: * which are by Jesus Christ, unto the glory and praise of God.
Our citizenship is in heaven: * from whence also we look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ.
May ye walk worthy of the Lord * unto all pleasing: being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God.
As the lightning cometh out of the east, * and shineth even unto the west: so shall the Coming of the Son of Man be.
As the lightning cometh out of the east, * and shineth even unto the west: so shall the Coming of the Son of Man be.

Let us celebrate the Conversion of Saint Paul the Apostle: for he, that was aforetime a persecutor, today became a chosen vessel: * wherefore Angels are gladsome, Archangels are jubilant, and unite in praising the Son of God in heaven.
In holiness and righteousness they served before the Lord God of Israel all the days of their life: * therefore hath he put upon them a robe of honour and a crown of glory.
Thus said the Lord unto Simon Peter: * Whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth, shall be bound in heaven, and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth, shall be loosed in heaven.

In the midst of the throne, and round about the throne, were four living creatures, having each of them six wings full of eyes on every side: and they rest not either by day or by night, saying: * Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God Almighty, which was, and which is, and which is to come, alleluia.
Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid: ye believe in God, believe also in me: * in my Father's house are many mansions, alleluia, alleluia.
After they had prayed, they gave forth their lots; and the lot fell upon Matthias: * and he was numbered with the eleven Apostles.
When Elizabeth * heard the salutation of Mary, she spake out with a loud voice, and said: Why is this granted me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me? alleluia.
Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends: * ye are my friends, saith the Lord.
The mouth of Zacharias * was opened, and he prophesied, saying: Blessed be the God of Israel.
reference: NATIVITY OF ST JOHN THE BAPTIST

content: Then Simon Peter * answered him, Lord, to whom shall we go? Thou hast the words of eternal life.
Because thou hast seen me, Thomas, thou hast believed: * blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed, alleluia.
Mary therefore * anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped them with her hair, and the house was filled with the odor of the ointment.
When Herod the king stretched forth his hands to do evil to certain of the Church: * he killed James, the brother of John, with the sword.
There shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse: * and all the earth shall be filled with the glory of the Lord, and all flesh shall see the salvation of our God.
And behold a voice * out of the cloud, which said, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him, alleluia.

On the iron grate, O God, I denied thee not; and when fire was kindled beneath me, O Christ, I confessed thee: * thou hast proved my heart and hast visited me in the night-season; thou hast tried me with fire, and hast found no wickedness in me.
Who is she that looketh forth as the morning: * fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and terrible as an army with banners?
Jesus said unto his Apostles, He that is greatest among you, let him be as the younger: * and he that is chief, as he that doth serve. I am among you as he that serveth.
Herod sent an executioner, and gave him commandment to behead John in the prison: * and when his disciples heard of it, they straightway came and took up his body, and laid it in a tomb.
Today let us celebrate, with duteous solemnity, the Nativity of God's all-holy Mother, the ever-Virgin Mary: * from whom the Son of the Highest proceeded, alleluia.
Thou alone * excellest in stature all the cedars of Lebanon: for on thee the Life of the world was hanged, on thee was Christ victorious, and death over death did forever triumph.
The Holy Apostle and Evangelist Saint Matthew preached not himself: * but the glorious Gospel of Christ, the Image of God, whose light dawneth upon us.
Blessed art thou, O Mary, for thou hast believed: * there shall be performed in thee the things which were told thee from the Lord.
There was silence in heaven * while the dragon waged war: and Michael fought against him, and had the victory, alleluia.
By his holy Gospel doth Saint Luke the Evangelist proclaim the tender mercy of our God: * whereby the Day-spring from on high hath visited us.
Jesus saith unto Saint Jude, If a man love me, he will keep my words, and my Father will love him:* and we will come unto him and abide with him.

The glorious company * of the Apostles praise thee; the goodly fellowship of the Prophets praise thee; the white robed army of Martyrs praise thee; with one heart and voice do all the elect acknowledge thee: O blessed Trinity, one only God.

Zacchaeus, make haste, and come down: * for today I must abide at thy house. And he made haste, and came down, and received him joyfully into his house. This day is salvation come to this house from the Lord.
The First-begotten of the dead, * and the Prince of the kings of the earth:  he hath made us to be a kingdom unto God and to his Father.  Alleluia.
reference: OUR LORD JESUS CHRIST, KING OF THE UNIVERSE

content: The Lord God * said unto the serpent, I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed:  it shall bruise thy head.  Alleluia.
The gate of Paradise by Eve to all was closed: * and by the Virgin Mary it is again set open.
Blessed art thou, * O Mary, for thou hast believed; and there shall be a performance in thee of those things which were told thee from the Lord, alleluia.
Blessed art thou, * O Mary, for thou hast believed; and there shall be a performance in thee of those things which were told thee from the Lord, alleluia.
Ye which have forsaken all, * and followed me, shall receive a hundred-fold, and shall inherit everlasting life.
Ye which have forsaken all, * and followed me, shall receive a hundred-fold, and shall inherit everlasting life.
For theirs is the kingdom of heaven, who have despised earthly pleasures, * and have won the rewards of the kingdom: and have washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb.
Except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die, it abideth alone: * but if it die, it bringeth forth much fruit.
O Lord Jesu Christ, my gracious Master, I pray thee receive my spirit in peace: * for it is now time for me to come to thee, and I greatly long to behold thee.
Behold, the Name of the Lord cometh from afar: * and his glory filleth all the earth.
reference: EVE OF THE FIRST SUNDAY OF ADVENT

content: Fear not Mary, thou hast found favour with the Lord: * behold, thou shalt conceive and bear a Son, alleluia.
The Saviour of the world shall arise as the sun: * and shall come down into the Virgin's womb, as the showers upon the grass, alleluia.
reference: EVE OF THE SECOND SUNDAY OF ADVENT

content: Blessed art thou, Mary, who hast believed: * there shall be performed in thee the things which were told thee from the Lord, alleluia.
Before me there was no God formed, nor shall there be after me: * for to me shall every knee be bowed, and my Name shall every tongue confess.
reference: EVE OF THE THIRD SUNDAY OF ADVENT

content: Go your way to John, and say ye: * The blind do see, and the deaf hear; the lepers are cleansed, and the lame do walk.
When the sun hath risen in the heavens, * ye shall see the King of kings proceeding from the Father: as a bridegroom out of his chamber.
reference: EVE OF THE SOLEMNITY OF THE NATIVITY

content: Today * the Christ is born; today hath a Savior appeared:  today on earth Angels are singing, Archangels rejoicing:  today the righteous exult and say, Glory to God in the highest.  Alleluia.
The heavenly portals are unfolded to Christ's martyr, blessed Stephen: * who of all the saintly throng is the first in order, and therefore he reigneth triumphant, crowned in heaven, alleluia.
In the midst of the congregation he opened his mouth; and the Lord filled him with the spirit of wisdom and understanding: * in a robe of glory he arrayed him, alleluia.
Then were innocent children * slain instead of Christ by a wicked ruler; the very sucklings were put to death:  spotless, they followed the Lamb himself, and say forever:  Glory be to thee, O Lord.
The Child Jesus tarried behind in Jerusalem, * and Joseph and his Mother knew not of it, supposing him to have been in the company: and they sought him among their kinsfolk and acquaintance.
reference: EVE OF THE FEAST OF THE HOLY FAMILY

content: The Child Jesus increased in wisdom and stature: * in the sight of God and man.
God, for his great love wherewith he loved us: * hath sent his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, alleluia.
reference: EVE OF THE SOLEMNITY OF MARY, THE HOLY MOTHER OF GOD

content: Heirs are we of a great mystery; * the womb of her that knew not man is become the temple of the God-head:  he, of a Virgin incarnate, suffereth no defilement; all the nations shall gather, saying Glory be to thee, O Lord.  Alleluia.
As many as received him, * to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his Name.
reference: EVE OF THE SECOND SUNDAY AFTER CHRISTMAS

content: Thine almighty Word, O Lord, * hath leaped down from heaven out of thy royal throne.
The Wise Men, beholding the star, said one to another: * This is the sign of a mighty King; forth fare we, and let us seek him; and let us offer him gifts, gold, incense, and myrrh.
reference: EVE OF THE SOLEMNITY OF THE EPIPHANY

content: From the East there came Wise Men to Bethlehem for to worship the Lord; * and when they had opened their treasures, they presented unto him precious gifts: gold, as to a mighty Monarch; incense, as to the true God; and myrrh, to foreshadow his burial,  alleluia.
The soldier baptizeth the King, the servant his Master, the Baptist his Redeemer: * the water of Jordan marvelled, the Dove bare witness, the Father's voice was heard, This is my beloved Son.
reference: EVE OF THE FEAST OF THE BAPTISM

content: The springs of water were hallowed * when Christ appeared in majesty before the world: draw ye water from the wells of salvation, for now is every creature sanctified by Christ our God.
Lo, Mary hath borne to us a Saviour, of whom when John beheld him he cried, saying: * Behold the Lamb of God, that taketh away the sin of the world, alleluia.
reference: EVE OF THE SECOND SUNDAY AFTER EPIPHANY

content: Now there was a marriage in Cana of Galilee: * and Jesus himself was there, with Mary his Mother.
The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: * repent ye, and believe in the Gospel.
reference: EVE OF THE THIRD SUNDAY AFTER EPIPHANY

content: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, * because he hath anointed me to preach the Gospel to the poor.

Blessed are ye, when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate from you, and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of Man's sake: * rejoice ye, and leap for joy; for behold, your reward is great in heaven.
reference: EVE OF THE FOURTH SUNDAY AFTER EPIPHANY

content: Blessed are the pure of heart, for they shall see God: * blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called the children of God.
Ye are the light of the world: * let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.
reference: EVE OF THE FIFTH SUNDAY AFTER EPIPHANY

content: And Jesus said unto Simon, Fear not; * from henceforth thou shalt catch men.
Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: * I am not come to destroy but to fulfil.
reference: EVE OF THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER EPIPHANY

content: Blessed be ye poor: for yours is the kingdom of God. Blessed are ye that hunger now: * for ye shall be filled.
There was a man in Jerusalem whose name was Simeon: * and the same man was righteous and devout, and awaiting the consolation of Israel; and the Holy Ghost was upon him.
reference: EVE OF THE FEAST OF THE PRESENTATION

content: When the parents brought in the Child Jesus, then Simeon took him up in his arms, and blessed God, saying: * Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace.
The Lord said unto Adam, * Of the tree which is in the midst of paradise thou shalt not eat, for in the day that thou eatest thereof, thou shalt surely die.
reference: EVE OF THE SUNDAY CALLED SEPTUAGESIMA

content: The householder spake to the labourers, saying: Why stand ye here all the day idle? They say unto him, Because no man hath hired us. * Go ye also into the vineyard, and whatsoever is right, that ye shall receive.
Arise, O Lord, wherefore sleepest thou? Awake, and cast us not away for ever: * wherefore hidest thou thy countenance, and forgettest our adversity and misery?
reference: EVE OF THE SUNDAY CALLED SEXAGESIMA

content: Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, * that the power of Christ may rest upon me.
Love your enemies, do good to them which hate you: * bless them which curse you, and pray for them which despitefully use you.
reference: EVE OF THE SUNDAY CALLED QUINQUAGESIMA

content: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, * and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.
Lay up for yourselves * treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt.
Then Joseph, being raised from sleep, did as the Angel of the Lord had bidden him: * and took unto him his wife.
reference: EVE OF THE SOLEMNITY OF ST JOSEPH

content: Good and faithful servant, * enter thou into the joy of thy Lord.
The Angel came in unto Mary, saying: * Hail, Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee.
reference: EVE OF THE SOLEMNITY OF THE ANNUNCIATION

content: O Virgin Mother of God, whence the Light Eternal hath deigned to dawn upon us: * regard, we pray thee, the pleading of thy humble servants, that by thy holy intercessions we may merit to obtain the mansions eternal.

Behold, now is the accepted time; behold now is the day of salvation: * let us therefore in these days approve ourselves as the servants of God, in much patience, in watchings, in fastings, and by love unfeigned.
reference: EVE OF THE FIRST SUNDAY IN LENT

content: Then the devil leaveth him: * and behold, angels came and ministered unto him.
Jesus taketh his disciples, and goeth up into a mountain, * and was transfigured before them.
reference: EVE OF THE SECOND SUNDAY IN LENT

content: Tell the vision which ye have seen to no man: * until the Son of Man be risen from the dead.
Whoso drinketh the water that I shall give him, saith the Lord, * it shall be in him a well of water, springing up unto everlasting life.
reference: EVE OF THE THIRD SUNDAY IN LENT

content: The hour cometh, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth; * for the Father seeketh such to worship him.
A man that is called Jesus made clay out of spittle: * and anointed mine eyes, and now I see.
reference: EVE OF THE FOURTH SUNDAY IN LENT

content: God so loved the world, that he gave his Only Begotten Son: * that whoso believeth in him should not perish, but have life everlasting.
Our friend Lazarus sleepeth: * let us go, that we may awake him out of sleep.
reference: EVE OF THE FIFTH SUNDAY IN LENT

content: Jesus answered and said, Now is the judgement of this world: * now shall the prince of this world be cast out. And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me.
Glorify me, O Father, * with thine own self: with the glory which I had before the world began.
For it is written, * I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered.  But after I am risen again, I will go before you into Galilee:  there shall you see me, saith the Lord.
As they were eating, * Jesus took bread, and blessed it, and brake it, and gave it to his disciples.
When he had received * the vinegar, he said, It is finished:  and he bowed his head, and gave up the ghost.
The chief priests and Pharisees made the sepulchre sure, * sealing the stone and setting a watch.
And when they looked, * they saw that the stone was rolled away: for it was very great.  Alleluia.
Behold, Jesus met the women, * saying, All hail; and they came and held him by the feet, and worshipped him, alleluia.
reference: MONDAY IN THE OCTAVE OF EASTER

content: Jesus saith unto her, * Touch me not; for I am not yet ascended to my Father, alleluia.
reference: TUESDAY IN THE OCTAVE OF EASTER

content: Did not our heart burn within us concerning Jesus: * while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the Scriptures? alleluia.
reference: WEDNESDAY IN THE OCTAVE OF EASTER

content: Behold my hands and my feet: * that it is I myself, alleluia.
reference: THURSDAY IN THE OCTAVE OF EASTER

content: This is now the third time * that Jesus showed himself: after that he was risen from the dead, alleluia.
reference: FRIDAY IN THE OCTAVE OF EASTER

content: After eight days, * when the doors were shut, the Lord entered, and said unto them:  Peace be unto you, alleluia, alleluia.
reference: EVE OF THE SECOND SUNDAY OF EASTER

content: The same day at evening, * being the first day of the week, and when the doors were shut where the disciples were assembled: Jesus stood in the midst of them, and said unto them: Peace be unto you, alleluia.
Abide with us, * for it is toward evening, and the day is far spent, alleluia.
reference: EVE OF THE THIRD SUNDAY OF EASTER

content: This is now the third time * that Jesus showed himself: after that he was risen from the dead, alleluia.
The Good Shepherd * goeth after the lost sheep and findeth it: and layeth it upon his shoulders, and bringeth it home, rejoicing, alleluia.
reference: EVE OF THE FOURTH SUNDAY OF EASTER

content: The Good Shepherd: * layeth down his life for his sheep, alleluia.
I am the Way, the Truth, and the Life: * no man cometh to the Father, but by me, alleluia.
reference: EVE OF THE FIFTH SUNDAY OF EASTER

content: A new commandment I give unto you, * That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another.
I will not leave you comfortless: * I go away, and come again to you; and your heart shall be joyful, alleluia.
reference: EVE OF THE SIXTH SUNDAY OF EASTER

content: If a man love me, * he will keep my words, and my Father will love him: and we will come unto him and abide with him, alleluia.
Father, I have manifested thy Name * unto the men whom thou hast given me: and now I pray for them, not for the world, because I come to thee, alleluia.
reference: EVE OF THE SOLEMNITY OF ASCENSION

content: O King of glory, * thou Lord of Sabaoth, who triumphing today hast ascended above all heavens, leave us not comfortless; but send on us the promise of the Father, even the Spirit of truth.  Alleluia.
So then the Lord Jesus, * after he had spoken unto them, ascended into heaven: and sitteth on the right hand of God, alleluia.
reference: EVE OF THE SEVENTH SUNDAY OF EASTER

content: These things have I told you, * that when the hour cometh: ye may remember that I told you of them, alleluia.
If a man love me, * he will keep my words, and my Father will love him: and we will come unto him, and make our abode with him, alleluia.

Today * are fulfilled the days of Pentecost, alleluia:  Today the Holy Spirit appeared in fire to the disciples, and bestowed upon them his manifold graces:  sending them into all the world, to preach the gospel, and to testify:  He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved.  Alleluia.
And when the days of Pentecost were fulfilled, * they were all with one accord saying Alleluia.
Thanks, O God, be unto thee, * thanks be unto thee: one and very Trinity, one and supreme Deity, holy and perfect Unity.
reference: EVE OF THE SOLEMNITY OF TRINITY

content: Thee, O God, * the Father unbegotten; thee, O only begotten Son; thee, O Holy Spirit, the Paraclete; holy and undivided Trinity:  with our whole heart and mouth we confess thee: to thee be glory for ever and ever.

O how sweet, O Lord, is thy Spirit, * who, to show thy loving-kindness to thy children, dost feed them with the sweetest Bread which came down from heaven: filling the hungry with good things, and sending the rich and disdainful empty away.
reference: EVE OF THE SOLEMNITY OF THE MOST HOLY BODY AND BLOOD

content: O sacred banquet, * wherein Christ is received, the memory of his Passion is renewed; the world with grace is filled, and a pledge of future glory is bestowed.  Alleluia.
I will speak of all thy marvellous works; * I will be glad, and rejoice in thee: yea, my songs will I make of thy Name, O most Highest.
The Lord, remembering his mercy, * hath clasped us to his breast and held us in his loving heart.  Alleluia.
I will sing of the Lord, * because he hath dealt so lovingly with me: yea, I will praise the Name of the Lord Most Highest.
I say unto you, * There is joy in the presence of the Angels of God: over one sinner that repenteth.
The Lord is my strong rock, * and my defence: my Saviour, my God, and my might.
One thing have I desired of the Lord, * which I will require: even that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life.
Therefore * I will offer in his dwelling an oblation with great gladness: I will sing, and speak praises unto the Lord.
Bow down thine ear to me: * make haste to deliver me.
O taste and see * how gracious the Lord is: blessed is he that putteth his trust in him.
He that eateth my Flesh, * and drinketh my Blood: dwelleth in me, and I in him.
Thou shalt be pleased * with the sacrifice of righteousness: with the burnt offerings and oblations upon thine altar, O Lord.
Honour the Lord with thy substance, * and with the first-fruits of all thine increase: so shall thy barns be filled with plenty, and thy presses shall burst out with new wine.

The earth, O Lord, * is filled with the fruit of thy works: that thou mayest bring food out of the earth, and wine that maketh glad the heart of man.  And oil to make him a cheerful countenance: and bread to strengthen man's heart.
Thou hast given us Bread from heaven, O Lord: * having every delight, and every taste of sweetness.
Seek ye first the kingdom of God: * and all those things shall be added unto you, saith the Lord.
The Bread that I will give * is my Flesh: which I will give for the life of the world.
O Lord, * I will make mention of thy righteousness only; thou, God, hast taught me from my youth up until now: forsake me not, O God, in my old age, when I am grey-headed.

Promise unto the Lord your God, * and keep it: all ye that are round about him bring presents unto him that ought to be feared.  He shall refrain the spirit of princes: and is wonderful among the kings of the earth.
Bring offerings, * and come into his courts: O worship the Lord in the beauty of holiness.
Thou hast charged * that we shall diligently keep thy commandments: O that my ways were made so direct, that I might keep thy statutes.
Remember thy word unto thy servant, O Lord, * wherein thou hast caused me to put my trust: the same is my comfort in my affliction.
My soul hath longed for thy salvation; * and I have a good hope in thy word: when wilt thou be avenged of them that persecute me?  They persecute me falsely: O be thou my help, O Lord my God.
I have called upon thee, O God, * for thou shalt hear me: incline thine ear unto me, and hearken unto my words.
Verily I say unto you, * what things soever ye desire, when ye pray: believe that ye receive them, and it shall be done unto you.
Out of the deep * have I called unto thee, O Lord: Lord, hear my voice.
Beloved, now are we the sons of God, * and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that when Christ shall appear, we shall be like him, for we shall see him as he is.

But when it pleased him, who separated me from my mother's womb, and called me by his grace and mercy, to reveal his Son in me among the nations: * immediately I conferred not with flesh and blood, neither went I to them that were Apostles before me.
These men are holy, for they are the very friends of God, and glorious heralds of divine truth: * their tongues were made the keys of the kingdom of heaven.
Thou art Shepherd of the sheep, and Prince of the Apostles; * God hath given unto thee, O Peter, the keys of the kingdom of heaven.
reference: EVE OF THE SOLEMNITY OF THE CHAIR OF SAINT PETER

content: This is he who wrought with great power before God, and all the earth is filled with his teaching: * may he intercede for the sins of all the people.
For the wisdom of the ancients the holy Evangelists searched with diligent enquiry: * and by the Prophets' sayings did they establish the truth of their narration, alleluia.
If ye had known me, ye should have known my Father also: * and from henceforth ye know him, and have seen him, alleluia.
In the regeneration, when the Son of Man sitteth upon the throne of his glory: * ye also will sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel, saith the Lord.
All generations * shall call me blessed:  for God hath regarded the lowliness of his handmaiden.  Alleluia.
Barnabas was a good man, and full of the Holy Spirit and of faith: * and much people was added unto the Lord.
When Zacharias went into the temple, there appeared unto him the Angel Gabriel: * standing on the right side of the altar of incense.
reference: EVE OF THE SOLEMNITY OF THE NATIVITY OF ST JOHN

content: The child * that is born unto us is more than a prophet; for this is he of whom the Saviour saith:  Among them that are born of women, there hath not risen one greater than John the Baptist.
reference: NATIVITY OF ST JOHN THE BAPTIST

content: Most illustrious of earth's Princes, forasmuch as in their lives they loved one another: * so also in death they were not divided.
reference: EVE OF THE SOLEMNITY OF STS PETER AND PAUL

content: Peter the Apostle, and Paul the Gentiles' teacher: * these have instructed us in thy law, O Lord.
O Thomas Didymus, through Christ who suffered thee to touch him, * we implore thee, by thy prayers for us on high, to aid us in our miseries, lest we be doomed with the lost when the Judge appeareth.
A woman * in the city, which was a sinner, brought an alabaster box of ointment, and stood at the Lord's feet, and began to wash his feet with tears, and did wipe them with the hairs of her head.
Jesus said unto James and John, Ye shall indeed drink of the cup that I drink of: * and with the baptism that I am baptised withal shall ye be baptised.
Rejoice, O glorious Matron, for thy prayers are heard: * thou hast borne the Mother of all our hopes, the Mother of Jesus, alleluia.
Tell the vision which ye have seen to no man: * until the Son of Man be risen from the dead.
reference: EVE OF THE FEAST OF THE TRANSFIGURATION

content: And when the disciples heard it, * they fell on their face, and were sore afraid:  and Jesus came and touched them, and said, Arise, and be not afraid.  Alleluia.

Blessed Lawrence, when laid and burning on the iron grating, spoke to the impious tyrant, saying, The feast is ready; turn and eat: * for the Church's treasures, which thou claimest, have been garnered up in heaven by the hands of the poor and needy.
Blessed is the lineage whence Christ proceeded:  how glorious is the Virgin who bare the King of heaven.
reference: EVE OF THE SOLEMNITY OF THE ASSUMPTION

content: Today the blessed Virgin went up into heaven: * rejoice ye, for with Christ she reigneth for ever and ever.
Jesus said unto his Apostles, I appoint unto you a kingdom: * and ye shall sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
The disciples of blessed John the Baptist came and took up his body: * and laid it in a tomb.
Let us celebrate the worshipful Nativity of the blessed and glorious Virgin Mary: * whose lowliness the Lord regarded, when, at the word of an Angel, she conceived the world's Redeemer, alleluia.
O blessed Cross, * which alone was counted worthy to bear the Lord and King of heaven.
reference: EVE OF THE FEAST OF THE EXALTATION OF THE HOLY CROSS

content: O Cross, * surpassing all the stars in splendor, world renowned, exceeding dear unto the hearts of men, holier than all things: thou only wert counted worthy to uphold the world's ransom.  Sweet the wood, sweet the iron, bearing so sweet a burden:  bring aid to this congregation, who are here assembled to celebrate thy praises.
God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts: * to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God, in the face of Jesus Christ.
All generations shall call me blessed: * for God hath regarded his lowly handmaiden.
O Prince most glorious, * Michael the Archangel, keep us in remembrance:  here and everywhere, always, entreat the Son of God for us.  Alleluia, alleluia.
In his holy Gospel, the beloved physician and Evangelist Saint Luke wrote of all that Jesus began both to do and to teach: * until the day in which he was taken up.
Ye are built upon the foundation of the Apostles and the Prophets: * Jesus Christ himself being the chief cornerstone.

Blessed are ye, O all ye Saints of God, who have been worthy to become companions of the heavenly powers, and to rejoice in the brightness of glory;* therefore, we pray you, that mindful of us you would vouchsafe to intercede for us unto the Lord our God.
reference: EVE OF THE SOLEMNITY OF ALL SAINTS

content: O how glorious is the kingdom wherein all the Saints rejoice with Christ; * arrayed in white robes, they follow the Lamb withersoever he goeth.

Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and the Spirit of God dwelleth within you: * for the temple of God is holy, which temple are ye; for the love of whom ye do this day celebrate the joys of the temple with a season of festivity.
The Lord God * shall give unto him the throne of his father David:  and he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever, and of his kingdom there shall be no end.  Alleluia.
reference: EVE OF THE SOLEMNITY OF OUR LORD JESUS CHRIST, KING

content: Upon his vesture and on his thigh his Name is written: * King of kings and Ruler of rulers. To him be glory and majesty for ever and ever.
reference: OUR LORD JESUS CHRIST, KING OF THE UNIVERSE

content: Hail, Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee;  blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb. Alleluia.
Blessed art thou among women: * and blessed is the Fruit of thy womb.
All generations shall call me blessed:  for God hath regarded his lowly handmaiden.

They will deliver you up * to the councils, and they will scourge you in their synagogues; and ye shall be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them and the Gentiles.

They will deliver you up * to the councils, and they will scourge you in their synagogues; and ye shall be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them and the Gentiles.

In the heavenly kingdom the souls of the Saints are rejoicing, who followed the footsteps of Christ their Master: * and since for love of Him they freely poured forth their life-blood, therefore with Christ they reign forever and ever.

This is indeed a Martyr who for the Name of Christ poured forth his life-blood: * who feared not the threats of judges, nor sought for the glory of earthly dignity, but with joy attained unto the heavenly kingdom.
O Wisdom, * which camest out of the mouth of the most High, and reachest from one end to another, mightily and sweetly ordering all things: Come and teach us the way of prudence.
title: Great O Antiphon

content: O Adonai, * and Leader of the house of Israel, who appearedst in the Bush to Moses in a flame of fire, and gavest him the law in Sinai:  Come and redeem us with an outstretched arm.
title: Great O Antiphon

content: O Root of Jesse, * which standest for an ensign of the people, at whom kings shall shut their mouths, to whom the Gentiles shall seek:  Come and deliver us, and tarry not.
title: Great O Antiphon

content: O Key of David, * and Sceptre of the house of Israel; that openest, and no man shutteth; and shuttest and no man openeth:  Come, and bring the prisoner out of the prison-house, and him that sitteth in darkness, and the shadow of death.
title: Great O Antiphon

content: O Dayspring, * Brightness of Light everlasting, and Sun of righteousness: Come, and enlighten them that sitteth in darkness, and the shadow of death.
title: Great O Antiphon

content: O King of the nations, * and their Desire; the Cornerstone, who makest both one:  Come, and save mankind, whom thou formedst of clay.
title: Great O Antiphon

content: O Emmanuel, * our King and Lawgiver, the Desire of all nations, and their Salvation:  Come and save us O Lord, our God.
title: Great O Antiphon
